blindSummary:
This country presents deep, institutionalised hostility toward trans visitors emanating from the head of state personally, now operating as state policy. Police profile and detain trans women for identity checks (20 were detained in the largest city in July 2025); trans women have historically been "frequent targets of torture and ill-treatment" by police, and a trans woman attacked with a knife was herself detained (the victim was criminalised). A draft law leaked in October 2025 would criminalise LGBT people — not yet passed but under active government consideration.

Transphobic attacks and Pride-event violence are documented, the health ministry is introducing regulations that may profile and restrict trans healthcare, and foreign visitors must carry original passports at all times — creating outing risk at the frequent checkpoints. If detained, trans women are placed in men's facilities with documented rights violations.

The risk is concentrated in urban trans-visible contexts (specific districts of the largest city known for trans socialising) rather than package-holiday tourist zones, but the institutional hostility pervades. The country lies outside the region's passport-free travel area.
blindOutOfScope: General terrorism and crime advisories affect all travellers here.
blindSourceSummaries: An international rights group (Oct 2025): a draft penal-code package in this country would threaten LGBT people with long prison terms, in effect criminalising them.

LGBTI+ organisation review (Feb 2026): a 'major siege' against LGBTI+ people in 2025 - hostility turned into state policy; the group's annual LGBTI+ human-rights report (framing the year as a 'major siege' against LGBTI+ people under a family-year theme) documents institutionalised anti-LGBTI policies, hate speech from senior officials, and instructions to public institutions under the government's family-year programme, creating a climate encouraging human-rights violations.

News site (Aug 2025): police in the largest city detain ~20 trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns - stopped on the street, while shopping or in cafés in a central district, held at a central police station and released after blanket identity-background checks; legal experts argue such general-information checks violate the right to liberty under the regional human-rights convention; one detainee reported being documented rather than fined, saying the new law 'hasn't even passed yet, but they're already enforcing it on us'. This signals enforcement in practice ahead of legislation.
News website (Feb 2026): report documents sharp rise in LGBTQ rights violations in this country in 2025 - coverage of the LGBTI+ organisation's report findings.

Monitoring report by seven human-rights organisations with a victim-blaming title (Aug 2025): documenting violations during and after the largest city's 11th trans pride march and 23rd LGBTI+ pride march during pride week; systematic violations ongoing since 2015, with senior officials using discriminatory rhetoric.

LGBTI+ organisation (Sept 2025): a new health ministry regulation may profile trans people and restrict transition access - 'gender reassignment' added to official reasons for medical board reports; e-reports replace paper; boards must now include six specialities examining applicants separately; the ministry says it 'does not grant a new right' but strengthens 'control and monitoring mechanisms'.

LGBTI+ organisation (Aug 2024): transphobic attack in the largest city - a trans woman was attacked with a knife by a 17-year-old in a city district; the victim was detained and spent the night in a detention centre while the attacker was released; the organisation notes that detaining the victim trans woman rather than the knife attacker reveals the state's hate policy.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (timeout); the underlying legal/travel-guidance site piece (2026) covers this country's passport-carrying rule, fines and detention warnings.

An international rights group (May 2008): a 123-page report documents this country's long, continuing history of violence and abuse based on sexual orientation and gender identity, urging urgent legal reform and that a regional union condition membership prospects on ending the abuses.
blindLocalsOnly: The health ministry's trans-healthcare regulations are resident-facing; the men's-facility placement of trans women concerns resident detainees.
